note: P-384 point arithmetic needs no signature, so the fixture's ACTUAL compiled locking script runs on @bsv/sdk's Spend engine with concrete points. Every expected point is OpenSSL's (crypto.createECDH('secp384r1') with the scalar as private key), NOT compiler output. The k=2 and P+P spends are the two defects fixed here: p384Mul(G,2n) returned 96 zero bytes and p384Add(G,G) returned a wrong point.

spends.note: p384Mul(G, 2) == 2G — the scalar that returned the all-zero point
p384MulGen(2) == 2G — same ladder, generator entry point
p384Add(G, G) == 2G — the affine doubling case that returned a wrong point
p384Mul(G, 3) == 3G != the committed 2G — proves the accepts are not vacuous
